subject: Audit: subprocessor segmentation and ephemeral-key custody for RetailBank pilot
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@retailbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@retailbank.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit: subprocessor segmentation and ephemeral-key custody for RetailBank pilot

Hi Karthik,

We're kicking off a short compliance sprint on the RetailBank pilot and need a compact evidence package focused on two areas: (1) a current subprocessor roster (with residency and KMS / HSM posture) and (2) your ephemeral-key custody model — specifically any escrow or BYOK options and whether you support HSM-backed key custody for Private deployments.

For the roster: please include the subprocessor name, country of operation, data categories processed, whether they have an attestation (SOC2 / ISO) and KMS ownership (Redwood-managed KMS, customer BYOK, or third-party HSM).

For keys: RetailBank's security team is particularly concerned about ephemeral key lifecycle for inference workloads and how we can prove non-persistence and control over long-term secrets. If you can provide a short statement (signed) about ephemeral-key handling and any third-party subprocessors that have access to key material, that would be ideal.

What we need by EOD Wednesday (08/12):
- Subprocessor CSV snapshot covering the current production and staging fleets
- SOC2 summary or link to your most recent report
- Short signed policy letter describing ephemeral-key handling and escrow options

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide HSM-backed BYOK for the pilot (or if the only option is Redwood KMS)? Also propose a 30-minute call to walk our security reviewer through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Senior Security Manager
RetailBank

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@retailbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit: subprocessor segmentation and ephemeral-key custody for RetailBank pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide everything on your list. High level:

- Subprocessor snapshot: attached CSV (redwood_subprocessor_snapshot_20260810.csv) with residency, data categories, and attestation flags.
- SOC2: attaching a short read-only summary (soc2-readonly-summary.pdf) and we can grant an NDA-backed access to the full report if needed.
- Ephemeral key policy: we can provide a signed letter outlining ephemeral-key lifecycle and escrow options.

On HSM / BYOK: for RetailBank pilot we can support two modes depending on deployment:
1) Hosted / Redwood API: Redwood-managed keys (our KMS) with strict ephemeral rotation and audit logging; subprocessors with access are limited to telemetry and no long-term key persistence.
2) Private (VPC/on-prem): BYOK with customer-provided HSM (Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, GCP Cloud HSM, or on-prem HSM) via a key-wrapping flow — Redwood never stores unwrapped key material.

Laura is copying a short technical matrix that enumerates each subprocessor's KMS posture; Ben will coordinate doc delivery and the signature.

Propose a 30-minute call on Wed 08/12 at 10:00 AM PST to run through the artifacts. If that works, we'll share a calendar invite and the signed policy letter by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Platforms
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_snapshot_20260810.csv (text/csv); soc2-readonly-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit: subprocessor segmentation and ephemeral-key custody for RetailBank pilot

Karthik / Ben — internal technical note and suggested artifacts for the customer. Copying the relevant parts of your message below for context.

> On Mon, Aug 10, 2026 at 12:03 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> > On HSM / BYOK: for RetailBank pilot we can support two modes depending on deployment:
> > 1) Hosted / Redwood API: Redwood-managed keys (our KMS) with strict ephemeral rotation and audit logging; subprocessors with access are limited to telemetry and no long-term key persistence.
> > 2) Private (VPC/on-prem): BYOK with customer-provided HSM (Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, GCP Cloud HSM, or on-prem HSM) via a key-wrapping flow — Redwood never stores unwrapped key material.

Technical appendix (to include in the evidence bundle):
- subproc_kms_matrix.xlsx (attached): columns = subprocessor_name | country | data_categories | attestation (SOC2/ISO) | kms_posture (redwood_kms / customer_byok / third_party_hsm) | last_attestation_date
- Ephemeral key lifecycle summary (one pager):
  - Key generation: ephemeral session keys created per-request batch inside the serving runtime, wrapped with a short-lived envelope key.
  - Envelope key management: envelope keys rotated per-hour; master root keys are rotated per our KMS policy and subject to audit controls.
  - No long-term persistence: inference inputs and ephemeral keys are not written to persistent storage; KV cache is secured and TTL-limited.
  - Subprocessor access: EdgeCache LLC (caching CDN) has telemetry-only access; it does not receive keying material. We do have a telemetry ingestion partner in EU with SOC2 Type II — see spreadsheet.

Action items for Ben / Karthik:
- Ben: upload the signed policy letter to Drive and attach to the calendar invite.
- Karthik: confirm the Wed 10:00 AM PST timeslot and send the invite to Alex + procurement.

Attachments: subproc_kms_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
